title: Thai Sour Curry with Prawns and Napa Cabbage
summary: A punchy, sour and salty Thai curry built on a pounded chilli paste, with crisp cabbage and plump prawns cooked briefly to keep everything fresh.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
palm sugar or light brown sugar
napa cabbage, cut into 5 cm pieces
raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

steps.title: Pound
steps.text: Pound ¾ tsp salt with 20 dried chillies in a mortar until flaked, then add 15 g fresh chillies, the turmeric, garlic and shallots, pounding well between each, and finally 30 g shrimp paste, until fine, about 15 min in total, or blend everything with 240 ml of the water until smooth.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk the paste with 240 ml water in a saucepan until smooth, then stir in the remaining water, 80 g tamarind paste, 12 g sugar and 3 tbsp fish sauce, and bring to the boil.

steps.title: Wilt
steps.text: Add 300 g napa cabbage and cook for 3-4 min until just wilted but still crisp-tender.

steps.title: Poach
steps.text: Add 400 g prawns, push under the liquid and cook until pink and opaque, 2-3 min.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Take off the heat and stir in 1 tbsp lime juice, tasting for a sour, salty and hot balance.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately in bowls with jasmine rice.

tips: Pounding the paste by hand in a mortar gives a better texture than blending, though a blender works well if you're short on time.
Don't overcook the cabbage; it should stay crisp-tender rather than soft.
Cook the prawns only until they turn pink and opaque right through, then take the pan off the heat straight away.
storage: This curry is best served the moment it's made, as the prawns and cabbage don't keep their texture well once cooled and reheated. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
